Let $C(t)$ denote the concentration of a drug in the bloodstream (in milligrams per liter), where $t\ge 0$ is the number of hours since dosing began. The graph of the first derivative $y={C}^{′}(t)$ of the function $C(t)$ intersects the $T$-axis at the points $t=3,$ $t=6,$ and $t=9,$ as shown above. Find all values of $t$ for which the concentration is increasing.

$t\in [0,$

{{field-3}}$)$
question.worked_solution:
First, we recall the following:

- If ${C}^{′}(t)=0$ for all $t\in (a,b)$, then $C(t)$ is constant on $(a,b).$

- If ${C}^{′}(t)>0$ on $(a,b)$, then $C(t)$ is increasing on $(a,b).$

- If ${C}^{′}(t)<0$ on $(a,b)$, then $C(t)$ is decreasing on $(a,b).$

From the above graph, we can see that ${C}^{′}(t)$ is positive on the intervals $[0,3)$ and $(6,9):$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14193353/assets/586fd368d9693df248c212465d9d3a43c6355dc56b224e3ba22d84950fd05f96.png)

Therefore, the concentration is increasing when $t\in [0,\,3\,)\text{ }⋃\text{ }(\,6,\,9\,).$
